title: indigo_agent_scheduler: replace the DEFER_GAIN threshold with a deferral strength where a higher value waits more
description:
Reported by the owner: 'defer for altitude gain works fine at 5%, at 0% is as before and at 100 is like at 0'. Cause: AGENT_SCHEDULER_SETTINGS.DEFER_GAIN (label 'Defer for altitude gain (%)', range 0-100) is a threshold - a task waits only when a later start raises its run quality by at least DEFER_GAIN points (indigo_agent_scheduler_plan.c defer_release). So 0 is off, 1 waits most, larger values wait less, and above about 50 nothing ever waits because real gains are limited by @altitude and twilight. The scale runs opposite to what the label and range suggest.

Owner's decision (option 2): turn it into a strength where a higher value waits more.
- Replace the item DEFER_GAIN with DEFER (AGENT_SCHEDULER_SETTINGS_DEFER_ITEM_NAME in indigo_names.h), 0-100, step 1, default 0, label such as 'Wait for a better slot (%)'. 0 = off (no deferral, exactly as today with DEFER_GAIN 0). Higher values wait for a slot nearer the culmination.
- Map the strength to the internal threshold in the agent, at one place, linearly: strength 1 -> 20 quality points, strength 100 -> 1 point (threshold = 20 - 19 * (strength - 1) / 99). Keep indigo_scheduler_plan_decide() / indigo_scheduler_plan_with_deferral() taking the threshold so the planning code and its unit tests stay unchanged; if a value must not be 0 at strength 100 make sure the minimum is 1 point. Behavior at every strength must be monotonic: a higher strength never waits less than a lower one in the guide's example.
- Saved configurations with DEFER_GAIN are not migrated (the setting is unreleased); an old value is ignored and DEFER starts at 0. State this in the ticket note.
- Update INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md (the 'Waiting for a better slot' section, the example table with the DEFER values that reproduce it - e.g. the strength that maps to 5 points, the 'Choosing a value' list rewritten for the new scale, the Settings table, every DEFER_GAIN mention), doc/SCHEDULER.md and indigo_docs/PROPERTIES.md.
- Tests: integration tests that used DEFER_GAIN switch to DEFER with the equivalent value; add a unit or integration case for the mapping (0 off, 1 -> 20, 100 -> 1, monotonic) and one showing that 100 defers at least as much as a middle value (the reported symptom).
- Increment the scheduler agent DRIVER_VERSION.

outcome.summary: Pass at 0c244ccb5b. Mapping: defer_threshold() (indigo_agent_scheduler.c:1561) returns 0 for strength <= 0, else 20 - 19*(s-1)/99 (1->20, 100->1, linear); the 0 path is unchanged: select_task still gates on the item value > 0 (line 1668) and plan_decide/plan_with_deferral treat 0 as off. All former DEFER_GAIN item uses (update_plan 2328, select_deferred 2460) go through defer_threshold(); remaining DEFER_GAIN/defer_gain names are only the planner's internal threshold and the unit test's planner threshold macro. indigo_names.h renamed to AGENT_SCHEDULER_SETTINGS_DEFER_ITEM_NAME "DEFER", tab-aligned with neighbours at tab width 2. Item 0-100 step 1 default 0, label 'Wait for a better slot (%)'. DRIVER_VERSION 0x0300001A -> 0x0300001B. PROPERTIES.md, INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md and doc/SCHEDULER.md updated; anchors #waiting-for-a-better-slot-defer resolve to the renamed heading; no stale DEFER_GAIN text. Independently verified with a scratch copy of the plan unit test linked to the built archive: threshold of strength 79 reproduces the guide table exactly (M31 18:20 94, M45 21:10 95, M42 23:00 95, M81 02:20 93, mean 94); strengths 95/96/100 give mean 97/96/97 with M42 at 22:40 92% from 96, matching the documented dip (accepted by the owner). New integration case deferral_strength_waits_longer_when_higher is meaningful (strengths 1/50/79/100 in one run, strictly later releases, 100 waits longest) and deterministic: site latitude 0, target on the equator at hour angle -2 h, quality is altitude-only (no Moon), so releases vary only by the 5-min grid phase; recorded run 45/80/100/115 min against bounds 35-60 and 105-125 leaves about 10 min margin each side, consecutive gaps about 20 min. Checks whitespace, unit and command-1 (132/132 including the new case) recorded on current HEAD; worktree clean. No defects found. Minor non-blocking: SETTINGS_DEFER_ITEM macro (line 121) uses one tab like its misaligned predecessor; the mapping is tested indirectly through release times rat

history.text: Reproducing: DEFER_GAIN 100 vs 5 through a temporary integration case

Reproduction before the fix (temporary integration cases in test_agent_scheduler.c, removed afterwards; target two hours before its culmination at two thirds of its transit altitude, upload_before_culmination()): DEFER_GAIN 5 -> reason 'Deferred waits until 09:40 UTC, nearer its culmination', plan lists 'deferred from', task not started; DEFER_GAIN 50 -> task started at once ('Starting task Deferred' 1, no 'deferred from'); DEFER_GAIN 100 -> task started at once, the same as 0. Confirms the report: 100 behaves like 0, the scale is a threshold running opposite to the label.
Updating the guide, SCHEDULER.md and PROPERTIES.md for DEFER
Check command-1 started: make -j8 -C indigo_drivers/agent_scripting -f ../../Makefile.drv all && make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler

Implementation: AGENT_SCHEDULER_SETTINGS.DEFER_GAIN replaced by DEFER (AGENT_SCHEDULER_SETTINGS_DEFER_ITEM_NAME, 0-100, step 1, default 0, label 'Wait for a better slot (%)'). Mapping in one static function defer_threshold() in indigo_agent_scheduler.c: 0 -> 0 (off, deferral path skipped exactly as DEFER_GAIN 0 before), strength 1..100 -> threshold = 20 - 19 * (strength - 1) / 99 (1 -> 20, 50 -> 10.6, 79 -> 5.03, 100 -> 1). Planning code and its unit tests unchanged (they still take the threshold; the unit test's local DEFER_GAIN macro is the planner threshold 5). DRIVER_VERSION 0x0300001A -> 0x0300001B. No migration: a saved DEFER_GAIN value in an existing configuration is ignored (no matching item) and DEFER starts at 0; the setting is unreleased.
Guide example: DEFER 79 (threshold 5.03) reproduces the table exactly (M31 18:20 94 %, M45 21:10 95 %, M42 23:00 95 %, M81 02:20 93 %, mean 94 %), checked with a scratch program linking the unchanged planner on the unit test's example (48.15 N, 2026-11-19, four 60-min Messier tasks) for every strength 0..100.
Monotonicity finding (needs owner decision): on the guide example the deferral grows with the strength from 0 to 95 (mean quality 66.9 % at 0, 88.8 % at 50, 94.3 % at 79, 97.1 % at 95; total hold time rising), but at 96-97 it drops (mean 95.9 %, total hold 755 vs 795 min) and recovers partly to 96.8 % at 100: M45 is held so late (21:40-22:40) that M42 starts right after it at 22:40 (92 %) instead of being held until 23:25 (98 %). This is the planner's per-decision greedy deferral, not the mapping; with the planner unchanged the ticket's 'monotonic at every strength in the guide's example' holds for 0..95 only. Strength 100 still defers much more than a middle value (50: mean 88.8 %, holds 525 min; 100: 96.8 %, 775 min). Documented in the guide's 'Choosing a value' and SCHEDULER.md 'Choosing the strength'. On the guide example, mean quality rises with DEFER up to 95 (97.1 %) but dips at 96-100 (95.9-96.8 %) because the planner decides one task at a time (M45 held later pushes M42 to start right after it). Strength 100 still waits much more than 50. Accept and document (current state), tune strength 100 to ~1.7 points, or open a separate planner ticket?
Owner: commit - accept the current state (option 1): the 96-100 dip on the guide example stays documented, no further mapping or planner change in this ticket.
Reviewer: checking guide example at DEFER 79 with a scratch copy of the plan unit test
